get.description: A folder's subfolders; at the root, one's own. `shared` lists what others opened to you.

post.description:
Duplicate the current version as an independent document in the same or another folder.

The copy gets its own Core file, its own resource and its own grants, so editing
it never touches the original's versions; the original keeps a reference to what
was duplicated.

delete.description: Delete a draft nobody has seen: only its owner, and only before it was ever submitted.

post.description:
Take a submitted dossier back before anyone has decided on it.

The submission snapshot stays in history; pending approval tasks are closed here at
once so nobody can decide on a dossier its owner has pulled back.
Close a dossier its owner gives up on. It stays readable, with its history.
Leaders file away settled dossiers (approved, rejected or cancelled); undoable.
Pass a request to someone else, where the step allows it.

get.description: Processes this person may open a dossier under.

post.description: Walk every scenario through the draft. Nothing is created, sent or published.

get.description:
What the draft changes compared with the version in force: its steps and each scenario.

Read-only rehearsal. Both sides are evaluated against today's organisation, so a difference
between them comes from the process and not from people having moved.
Why a dossier went where it did: what was pinned at each submission, and Core's trace.
People and units this user may give work to, so the form offers only valid choices.

post.description: A download ticket for a file attached to a task, for anyone who may see the task.
Store a file for a message about to be sent; it stays private to the uploader until then.
Store a picture or video for a post about to be published; private to the uploader until then.

get.description: What needs this user now: counts for the menu and one agenda across modules.

The plugin finished a long-running step; only the first report counts.

patch.description:
Fill form fields the manifest declared in `writes.fields` and the administrator approved.

The dossier's status does not change; earlier submissions keep their snapshot.

post.description: A task given by the viewer, within whom and which units they may assign to.
Move a task by the same rules as in the app: only what the viewer may do at its status.
In-app notices to people or a unit, titled with the plugin's name.
Check a flow while it is being drawn; problems come back tied to their node.
Dry run of an unsaved flow: the path it would take; writes nothing and calls nothing.
Dry run of the saved flow for a sample event.

get.description: Records a manual run can use: those of the trigger's kind that the user may see.

post.description:
Run the saved flow now, for real, as if its event had just happened to that record.

Works whether the flow is switched on or not: it is how a flow is tried on real data,
or applied to a record that existed before the flow was made.
Ask a service which models it offers, using the stored key when the form leaves it blank.
What the assistant would read for a question, without calling any AI service.
1. Read an attached file and propose a value, with page and quote, for each field.
2. A few lines for the approver: what is asked, how much, what is attached, who said what.
3. Before submitting: what might be wrong, from fixed rules and from the attachments.
4. A polite approval note or return reason, for the person deciding to edit.
Questions about the dossier open on screen, answered from that dossier only.
5. Turn a few points into an administrative document laid out per Decree 30.
6a. A short summary of a document, each point with the page it comes from.
6b. Answer a question from the document only, quoting the page it rests on.
7. Items whose content means what was asked, only those this person may open.
8. Labels and a folder that fit a document, from the labels and folders already in use.
9. Fill the assign-work form from one sentence; the person still reviews and presses Assign.
10. Steps or sub-tasks for a large task, with suggested due dates before the task's own.
11. This morning in words: what is urgent, what waits for approval, what is about to slip.
12. The report page in words, with where things stall and what to look at.
13. What a long conversation said and agreed, from the messages this member can read.
14a. Rewrite a post more concisely, fix spelling, or suggest titles.
14b. A text alternative for an image the author is posting, saved on the attachment.
17. Scenarios worth testing (amounts at the threshold, missing files) with their real result.

FileCopy.title: FileCopy
FileCopy.description:
Duplicate a document the caller can already read.

No revision is taken on the source: copying changes nothing about it. An
Idempotency-Key is required instead, because a retried copy would otherwise create a
second independent document.
